newsitem.title: ITALY: Iri Spa debt falls in 1996, sees profit.
newsitem.headline: Iri Spa debt falls in 1996, sees profit.

text.p: Italian industrial state holding Iri Spa said in a statement it had returned to profit in 1996 while its debt level fell to about 9.5 trillion lire from 22.5 trillion lire previously.

"Preliminary data for 1996 show a return to a positive result for Iri Spa, registering a slight profit and an improvement of more than 2.0 trillion lire in respect to budget forecasts," an Iri statement said.
It said the preliminary results took account of the capital gain made to date through the transfer of its stake in state telecommunications holding Stet to the Italian Treasury.
It said consolidated results showed the Iri group had made a limited loss, reflecting the exit of the telecoms unit from the group.
Iri debt at the end of 1996 had fallen 13.0 trillion to about 9.5 trillion lire.
"The debt level at the end of 1996 is now near to the level seen as acceptable in agreements between the Italian government and the European Union," it said.

The company said its 1997 budget envisaged a breakeven at both parent and group level, saying there was "a definite possibility of confirming breakeven levels and a stable financial position, without taking into account possible adjustments over the Stet divestment."
